done_when: While a child close waits only for checks, land --all releases its slot so another item can start, keeping stack and shared-file order, and a test shows a waiting child does not block a new close

known.title: Forward the check-slot callback through the behind-base retry

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. The callback is forwarded through conflict recovery here, but the other recovery call to `close.close` at src/forge/merge.py:130–133 drops `check_slot`. When another pull request advances main and GitHub rejects the merge as BEHIND, that refreshed close pushes a new head and waits for its checks with `slot=None` (src/forge/close.py:427–430). It consequently holds its queue slot throughout running CI, blocking independent closes again when the queue is saturated. Forward the callback through that Namespace too. The new test never triggers a rejected merge followed by this recovery, so it misses this path.
findings.title: Forward the check-slot callback through the behind-base retry

why: forge land --all holds its slots while its child closes only wait for GitHub checks, so other items cannot start closing
